title: Cross & Derry
standfirst: A baptism at South Leith is documented in 1686. The proposed move to Cross and the later Derry/Tyrone descent have not been bridged by an Irish record.
question: Can Irish records bridge Charles Glasgow from the Scottish baptism to the Cross families?
answer: No reviewed record carries the South Leith child to Ireland or names him in the Cross families. Later Cross, Killycurragh and Ballynasollus material is useful for local research, but it is not a documented chain from Charles.

chapters.title: A recorded Scottish baptism
body: Charles Glesgowe was baptised at South Leith on 10 October 1686, the son of John Glesgowe and Margaret Currie.
That record is direct evidence for the baptism only; its original image still needs inspection and it says nothing about a later Irish life.

chapters.title: The missing bridge
body: The surviving Derryloran and Cookstown baptism registers begin too late to document the proposed early move. Searches of the reviewed will and deed indexes have not located Charles at Cross.
Those bounded negative results do not disprove a migration; they leave the identity and every intervening relationship unproved.

chapters.title: Later families remain leads
body: David's reported Irish birth and Indiana death come from a contributed tree, not an inspected record. James represents later Cross-area material, not proof of descent from Charles.
Each later household needs its own records before it can be connected to another subgroup.

clusters.title: Charles of South Leith
clusters.summary: A baptism names Charles and his parents in South Leith.
clusters.boundary: It does not identify a man at Cross or establish migration.

clusters.summary: Later displayed families offer places and names for record-led work.
clusters.boundary: No inspected record joins either household to Charles or to each other.

links.label: No record-defined migration or descent bridge

supported: A real later surname presence around Cross and neighbouring localities.
hypothesis: The baptised Charles was the later Cross man.
unresolved: Migration, spouse, children and every connecting generation.

gaps.title: Find the first Cross household record
gaps.why: A parish, lease, probate or land record could name Charles, relatives or a prior residence.

gaps.title: Inspect the baptism original
gaps.why: It confirms the exact Scottish record before any identity comparison.

gaps.title: Document the later households independently
gaps.why: This avoids turning locality and surname into descent.
gaps.where: Parish, census, probate and land records
